content.text:
Black Friday flight is over. Recap:

**What ran**
- Campaign "Quillstep Black Friday 2026" (account Quillstep, UK), 20–29 Nov 2026, WEBSITE_CLICKS objective, ALL_ON_TWITTER, funded by Visa ••8808. No X pixel exists, so sign-ups can't be tracked in-platform — link clicks were the proxy; actual sign-up count isn't measurable from ads data.
- Two line items, both promoting the 4 approved posts: **LI-A** UK + "Technology / Software Development" interest ($35/day → $20/day on 24 Nov, paused 27 Nov — clicks cost ~$5.4 each); **LI-B** UK broad ($20/day → $35/day on 24 Nov → $55/day on 27 Nov — clicks ~$2.6 each).
- Top creatives by clicks: post 2121392666835189657 (war-room/60-day trial) and post 2121936248635585410 (£0 Solo free forever); post 2121755054700018547 (deadline urgency) trailed.

**Results (full flight, per ads stats)**
- Spend: **$522.77** of $550 budget
- Impressions: **362,175** (LI-A 90,371 / LI-B 271,804)
- Link clicks: **161** (LI-A 36 / LI-B 125), ~$3.25 per link click; reach ~333k, avg frequency 1.09

**Notes / caveats**
- Sign-ups can't be attributed without a pixel; if you can pull sign-up counts for the flight window from your backend, comparing against the 161 clicks would tell you the true conversion rate.
- LI-A (interest-targeted) was consistently worse on cost per click than broad UK targeting and was paused on 27 Nov; remaining budget went to LI-B.
- Campaign and line items are now paused/ended; nothing is serving.
